categories.main_business_segments: The company operates primarily in three segments: MVNO (Mobile Virtual Network Operator) telecommunications services under the brand 'Pretty', smart grid business including AMI (Advanced Metering Infrastructure) systems and PLC chip manufacturing, and distribution/manufacturing including watches, cosmetics, health supplements, and alcoholic beverages. It also has subsidiaries engaged in fire alarm device manufacturing and other related businesses.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: Key technologies include AMI systems for smart grids utilizing PLC (Power Line Communication) chips developed in-house, firmware for power line communication modems, and proprietary telecommunication adapter technologies. The company outsources production for cosmetics and smart grid products and holds patents related to communication systems, smart power management, graphene coating, and stem cell-based biomedical products.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Primary customers include individual consumers for MVNO telecommunications services, utility companies such as Korea Electric Power Corporation for smart grid solutions, and retail consumers for cosmetics, health supplements, watches, and alcoholic beverages. The smart grid business targets public sector projects, while the MVNO segment serves a broad consumer base through retail and online channels.
categories.geographic_coverage: The company operates mainly in South Korea, with its headquarters and offices located in Seoul. It serves the domestic market extensively, especially in telecommunications and smart grid sectors, and exports some products such as cosmetics and watches. The smart grid technology and PLC chips have potential export plans, but the core operations are domestic.
categories.supply_chain_position: The company operates primarily as a downstream service provider in telecommunications by leasing network capacity from major MNOs and reselling services as an MVNO. In the smart grid segment, it develops core hardware and software components, positioning itself in midstream manufacturing and system integration. For distribution businesses, it acts as a retailer and wholesaler sourcing products from manufacturers and suppliers.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Strategic priorities include expanding the MVNO subscriber base, advancing smart grid technologies especially AMI and PLC chip development, and entering new growth areas such as NFTs, secondary batteries, electric two-wheelers, and data center infrastructure software. R&D efforts focus on communication adapters, smart power management, graphene applications, and biomedical innovations like stem cell therapies. The company also pursues digital transformation and new business models linked to its existing brands.
categories.revenue_model: Revenue is generated mainly through telecommunications service fees from MVNO operations, sales of smart grid hardware and software solutions, and retail sales of cosmetics, health supplements, watches, and alcoholic beverages. The company also earns from maintenance contracts in smart grid systems and plans to develop revenue streams from emerging businesses like NFTs and data center software solutions.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: In the MVNO market, the company competes with subsidiaries of major telecom operators and new entrants including financial institutions. The smart grid segment faces competition from established electrical and ICT companies with high entry barriers due to technical standards and certification requirements. In distribution, competition is intense in cosmetics and health supplements, with foreign brands dominating the watch market. The company maintains a stable position in MVNO and smart grid sectors leveraging technology and government projects.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: As of 2023, the company reported consolidated revenues of approximately 998 billion KRW, marking a 30.2% increase from the previous year, driven mainly by MVNO growth and smart grid sales. Total assets stood at about 765 billion KRW with liabilities around 381 billion KRW. Despite revenue growth, the company recorded a net loss due to investment losses in its bio subsidiaries. The MVNO segment is the cash cow, showing steady subscriber and ARPU growth, while smart grid and ICT segments are expanding with new contracts and R&D investments.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: The company differentiates itself by offering cost-effective MVNO services leveraging leased networks to provide competitive pricing and diverse plans. In smart grids, it provides domestically developed, certified PLC chip technology and integrated AMI solutions tailored to national utility projects. Its distribution brands focus on niche markets with targeted branding and product innovation, such as stem cell-based therapies and NFT-linked watch products. The company emphasizes technological innovation, government project alignment, and multi-segment diversification to create unique customer value.
